q: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the ____ is.
e: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the reaction is. Reaction is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: To describe the quantitative measurement of a reaction rate, it is necessary to specify how fast the reactants are used up or the ____ are formed.
e: To describe the quantitative measurement of a reaction rate, it is necessary to specify how fast the reactants are used up or the products are formed. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the ____ taken for that change.
e: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the time taken for that change. Time is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The reaction rate is usually expressed as the change in the amount of a reactant used up or the product formed in a unit of ____.
e: The reaction rate is usually expressed as the change in the amount of a reactant used up or the product formed in a unit of time. Time is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in ____.
e: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in volume. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: ____ units are used if the reactant or product is in solution.
e: Concentration units are used if the reactant or product is in solution. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Generally, in chemical reactions, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured in terms of a decrease in the concentration of the reactant or an increase in the concentration of the product per unit time at a constant ____.
e: Generally, in chemical reactions, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured in terms of a decrease in the concentration of the reactant or an increase in the concentration of the product per unit time at a constant temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: In the rate equation, the delta ($\Delta$) means ____.
e: In the rate equation, the delta (delta) means change. Change is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the rate equation, the square bracket [] represents molar ____.
e: In the rate equation, the square bracket [] represents molar concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The minus (-) sign means a ____ in the concentration of the reactant.
e: The minus (-) sign means a decrease in the concentration of the reactant. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: The plus (+) sign means an ____ in the concentration of the product.
e: The plus (+) sign means an increase in the concentration of the product. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Rate is expressed as a ____ quantity.
e: Rate is expressed as a positive quantity. A positive enthalpy change means the system absorbed heat.

q: In a general chemical reaction, a, b, c, and d are the stoichiometric ____ of the reactants and products in the balanced chemical equation.
e: In a general chemical reaction, a, b, c, and d are the stoichiometric coefficients of the reactants and products in the balanced chemical equation. Coefficients is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The rate constant, k, explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the ____ of a chemical reaction.
e: The rate constant, k, explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the rate of a chemical reaction. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in ____ of products and reactants.
e: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in concentrations of products and reactants. Concentrations is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid giving off ____ gas.
e: Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid giving off hydrogen gas. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: The volume of hydrogen gas released in the process of reaction at time intervals can be ____.
e: The volume of hydrogen gas released in the process of reaction at time intervals can be measured. Measured is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or ____).
e: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or years). Years is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: ____ theory explains how chemical reactions occur.
e: Collision theory explains how chemical reactions occur. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Collision theory is based on the kinetic molecular theory of ____.
e: Collision theory is based on the kinetic molecular theory of gases. Collision theory says particles must hit with the right orientation and enough energy or no reaction happens.

q: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess ____ energy.
e: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess kinetic energy. Kinetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction ____.
e: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: For a reaction to occur, colliding particles must possess a certain minimum energy known as an ____ energy.
e: For a reaction to occur, colliding particles must possess a certain minimum energy known as an activation energy. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need to react.

q: During a collision, the spatial ____ of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs.
e: During a collision, the spatial orientation of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will ____ off each other.
e: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will bounce off each other. Bounce is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a ____.
e: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a reaction. Reaction is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When the particles collide with the correct orientation, they must have enough energy for a successful collision (____ collision) to produce a reaction.
e: When the particles collide with the correct orientation, they must have enough energy for a successful collision (effective collision) to produce a reaction. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant ____.
e: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant particles. Particles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated ____.
e: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated complex. Complex is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The activated complex is a temporary species formed by the reactant particles as a result of the collision before they form the ____.
e: The activated complex is a temporary species formed by the reactant particles as a result of the collision before they form the product. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being ____.
e: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being faster. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: In the molecular view of the matter, it is postulated that chemical reactions depend on the collisions between the reacting particles - atoms, molecules or ____.
e: In the molecular view of the matter, it is postulated that chemical reactions depend on the collisions between the reacting particles - atoms, molecules or ions. Ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Reacting particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy ____ to react.
e: Reacting particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier to react. Barrier is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision ____.
e: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision increases. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy that is greater than the activation energy ____.
e: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy that is greater than the activation energy increases. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors such as concentration, temperature, pressure, and particle ____, affecting the rate of chemical reactions.
e: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors such as concentration, temperature, pressure, and particle size, affecting the rate of chemical reactions. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The activation energy ($E_a$) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful collision to take place in a ____.
e: The activation energy (Ea) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful collision to take place in a reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate which is known as an activated complex, having required minimum energy, is formed before producing a ____.
e: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate which is known as an activated complex, having required minimum energy, is formed before producing a product. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy ____ state.
e: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy transition state. Transition metals have a partly filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion.

q: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in this state is equal to the activation energy ($E_a$) for that ____.
e: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in this state is equal to the activation energy (Ea) for that reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: Hence, the activation energy represents an energy ____ for the reaction, and it has a different value in different reactions.
e: Hence, the activation energy represents an energy barrier for the reaction, and it has a different value in different reactions. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: In an exothermic reaction, since the final product has ____ energy than that of the reactants, energy is released.
e: In an exothermic reaction, since the final product has less energy than that of the reactants, energy is released. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: Some energy is released when the activated complex leads to the formation of the ____.
e: Some energy is released when the activated complex leads to the formation of the products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: When there is sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier, the formation of the product is ____.
e: When there is sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier, the formation of the product is favourable. Favourable is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If the energy is not enough, it cannot overcome the energy barrier and the decomposition of the product, that is, back to reactants will ____.
e: If the energy is not enough, it cannot overcome the energy barrier and the decomposition of the product, that is, back to reactants will occur. Occur is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A high $E_a$ means that relatively few collisions have the required energy to produce the activated complex, and hence, the reaction rate is ____.
e: A high Ea means that relatively few collisions have the required energy to produce the activated complex, and hence, the reaction rate is slow. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: With a low $E_a$, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is ____.
e: With a low Ea, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is fast. Fast is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate $[H_2I_2]$ which exists for a short time and then breaks up to form two molecules of hydrogen ____.
e: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate [H2I2] which exists for a short time and then breaks up to form two molecules of hydrogen iodide. Iodide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: For many reactions involving liquids or gases, increasing the concentrations of the reactants ____ the rate of reactions.
e: For many reactions involving liquids or gases, increasing the concentrations of the reactants increases the rate of reactions. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: The effect of concentration on the rate of reaction can be explained by the ____ theory.
e: The effect of concentration on the rate of reaction can be explained by the collision theory. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: If more molecules or ions of the reactants are in the reaction area, then there is a greater chance of more effective collisions per unit ____.
e: If more molecules or ions of the reactants are in the reaction area, then there is a greater chance of more effective collisions per unit time. Time is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In reactions involving solids, a reaction occurs at the boundary ____ between reactants.
e: In reactions involving solids, a reaction occurs at the boundary surface between reactants. Surface is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The rate of a reaction involving a solid reactant is increased by increasing the surface ____ of the solid.
e: The rate of a reaction involving a solid reactant is increased by increasing the surface area of the solid. Area is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The smaller the particle size, the larger the surface ____ will be.
e: The smaller the particle size, the larger the surface area will be. Area is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Reducing the size of particles increases the surface area, increases the number of collisions per second, increases the number of effective collisions, and thus increases the rate of ____.
e: Reducing the size of particles increases the surface area, increases the number of collisions per second, increases the number of effective collisions, and thus increases the rate of reaction. A larger surface area gives more places to collide, so a powdered solid usually reacts faster than a lump.

q: Changing the pressure does not affect the rate of reaction that only involves solids or ____.
e: Changing the pressure does not affect the rate of reaction that only involves solids or liquids. Liquids is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pressure affects the rate of a reaction involving ____.
e: Pressure affects the rate of a reaction involving gases. Gases is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Increasing the pressure increases the ____ of the reaction.
e: Increasing the pressure increases the speed of the reaction. Speed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The pressure is inversely proportional to the volume of a gas at a constant ____.
e: The pressure is inversely proportional to the volume of a gas at a constant temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: At low pressure, the volume becomes larger, the number of collisions of gaseous molecules is smaller, and thus, the rate of reaction is ____.
e: At low pressure, the volume becomes larger, the number of collisions of gaseous molecules is smaller, and thus, the rate of reaction is slower. Slower is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: At high pressure, the volume becomes smaller, the number of collisions is greater, and thus, the rate of reaction is ____.
e: At high pressure, the volume becomes smaller, the number of collisions is greater, and thus, the rate of reaction is faster. Faster is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Most chemical reactions react faster at a high temperature than at a low ____.
e: Most chemical reactions react faster at a high temperature than at a low temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: The kinetic energy of a gas is directly proportional to the ____.
e: The kinetic energy of a gas is directly proportional to the temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: Increasing the temperature also increases the kinetic energy, which means that the molecules move faster and collide more frequently with sufficient activation energy for the reaction to ____.
e: Increasing the temperature also increases the kinetic energy, which means that the molecules move faster and collide more frequently with sufficient activation energy for the reaction to proceed. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: The effect of temperature on reaction rates can also be explained by using the energy distribution curve also known as the ____ distribution.
e: The effect of temperature on reaction rates can also be explained by using the energy distribution curve also known as the Boltzmann distribution. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: In general, the area under the Boltzmann distribution curve represents the number of particles within a certain energy ____.
e: In general, the area under the Boltzmann distribution curve represents the number of particles within a certain energy range. Range is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The shaded area under the curve shows the number of particles with energy greater than the activation ____.
e: The shaded area under the curve shows the number of particles with energy greater than the activation energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: When the temperature is increased, the shape of the distribution curve flattens and spreads out, showing that the fraction of molecules with energy greater than $E_a$ is much ____ at the higher temperature.
e: When the temperature is increased, the shape of the distribution curve flattens and spreads out, showing that the fraction of molecules with energy greater than Ea is much larger at the higher temperature. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Generally, for a ten degrees rise in temperature, the area under the curve approximately doubles as does the ____ of reactions.
e: Generally, for a ten degrees rise in temperature, the area under the curve approximately doubles as does the rate of reactions. Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy to react.

q: A catalyst is defined as a substance which alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically ____ at the end of the reaction.
e: A catalyst is defined as a substance which alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Most catalysts make chemical reactions go ____.
e: Most catalysts make chemical reactions go faster. Faster is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Catalysts that make chemical reactions go faster are known as ____ catalysts.
e: Catalysts that make chemical reactions go faster are known as positive catalysts. A positive enthalpy change means the system absorbed heat.

q: Sometimes, a chemical reaction needs to go more slowly or suppress unwanted reactions using a ____ catalyst.
e: Sometimes, a chemical reaction needs to go more slowly or suppress unwanted reactions using a negative catalyst. A negative sign marks heat leaving the system, or a falling concentration, depending on the equation.

q: Generally, the catalysts provide an alternative pathway for the reaction with lower activation energy, and thus increasing the reaction ____.
e: Generally, the catalysts provide an alternative pathway for the reaction with lower activation energy, and thus increasing the reaction rate. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: Catalysts may be homogeneous, that is, uniformly mixed with the reactants, or heterogeneous, in which case the catalyst and the reactants are in different ____.
e: Catalysts may be homogeneous, that is, uniformly mixed with the reactants, or heterogeneous, in which case the catalyst and the reactants are in different phases. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Homogeneous catalysts most often catalyse the gaseous and aqueous reactions to increase their reaction ____.
e: Homogeneous catalysts most often catalyse the gaseous and aqueous reactions to increase their reaction rates. A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants.

q: Most heterogeneous catalysts are solids that catalyse either gaseous or liquid ____.
e: Most heterogeneous catalysts are solids that catalyse either gaseous or liquid reactants. Reactants appear on the left and in the denominator of K.

q: In heterogeneous catalysis, the reactions take place on the surface of the solid catalyst to speed ____.
e: In heterogeneous catalysis, the reactions take place on the surface of the solid catalyst to speed up. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Catalysts are important for the proper functioning of the biological ____.
e: Catalysts are important for the proper functioning of the biological systems. Systems is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Enzymes act as biocatalysts for specific biochemical reactions in living ____.
e: Enzymes act as biocatalysts for specific biochemical reactions in living systems. Systems is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In general, the reaction rate using enzymes is much faster than inorganic catalysts, often increased by a factor of $10^6$ to ____.
e: In general, the reaction rate using enzymes is much faster than inorganic catalysts, often increased by a factor of 106 to 1012. 1012 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Some chemical reactions obtain the energy they need from ____.
e: Some chemical reactions obtain the energy they need from light. Burning wood gives out heat and light as chemical energy is released.

q: Reactions that are initiated by light are called photochemical ____.
e: Reactions that are initiated by light are called photochemical reactions. A photochemical reaction starts when molecules absorb light energy.

q: The brighter the light, the faster is the ____.
e: The brighter the light, the faster is the reaction. Reaction is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If the intensity of light (visible or ultraviolet) is greater, the more reactant molecules gain the energy to absorb the ____.
e: If the intensity of light (visible or ultraviolet) is greater, the more reactant molecules gain the energy to absorb the light. Burning wood gives out heat and light as chemical energy is released.

q: When molecules absorb the light ($h\nu$), a photochemical reaction takes place, such as photosynthesis in green ____.
e: When molecules absorb the light (h), a photochemical reaction takes place, such as photosynthesis in green plants. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Storage of preserved foods at a sub-zero temperature is effective in slowing the rate of bacterial ____.
e: Storage of preserved foods at a sub-zero temperature is effective in slowing the rate of bacterial decay. Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy to react.

q: When large amounts of flammable powdered substances collect in grain elevators, coal mines and chemical industries, violent explosions can ____.
e: When large amounts of flammable powdered substances collect in grain elevators, coal mines and chemical industries, violent explosions can occur. Occur is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: At high altitudes with low temperature and low pressure, it takes a long time to ____ an egg.
e: At high altitudes with low temperature and low pressure, it takes a long time to boil an egg. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Corrosion inhibitors like imidazoline and quaternary amine prevent $H_2S$ and $CO_2$ ____.
e: Corrosion inhibitors like imidazoline and quaternary amine prevent H2S and CO2 corrosion. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Volatile corrosion inhibitors (VCI) such as morpholine or hydrazine prevent corrosion in ____.
e: Volatile corrosion inhibitors (VCI) such as morpholine or hydrazine prevent corrosion in boilers. Boilers is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Wrapping metals in volatile corrosion inhibitor-coated paper is common for short-term protection against moisture and ____.
e: Wrapping metals in volatile corrosion inhibitor-coated paper is common for short-term protection against moisture and humidity. Humidity is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Zinc granule reacts fairly slowly with dilute hydrochloric acid but much faster with the more concentrated hydrochloric acid as a function of ____.
e: Zinc granule reacts fairly slowly with dilute hydrochloric acid but much faster with the more concentrated hydrochloric acid as a function of time. Time is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Aluminium foil reacts moderately with sodium hydroxide solution only when warmed, but powdered aluminium of the same mass reacts rapidly in the ____.
e: Aluminium foil reacts moderately with sodium hydroxide solution only when warmed, but powdered aluminium of the same mass reacts rapidly in the cold. Cold is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Large pieces of wood are difficult to ignite whereas small pieces burn more ____.
e: Large pieces of wood are difficult to ignite whereas small pieces burn more rapidly. Rapidly is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Food can cook faster in a pressure cooker than in a pot, because trapped steam becomes hotter as the pressure ____.
e: Food can cook faster in a pressure cooker than in a pot, because trapped steam becomes hotter as the pressure increases. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: The time required to hard-boil an egg in water is much shorter at 100°C than at ____.
e: The time required to hard-boil an egg in water is much shorter at 100°C than at 80°C. 80°C is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Foods are cooled or frozen to slow down the chemical reactions that result in the spoiling of ____.
e: Foods are cooled or frozen to slow down the chemical reactions that result in the spoiling of food. Food is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the manufacturing process of sulphuric acid, nitrogen oxide acts as a catalyst in the oxidation of sulphur ____.
e: In the manufacturing process of sulphuric acid, nitrogen oxide acts as a catalyst in the oxidation of sulphur dioxide. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: In the ammonia oxidation process (Ostwald process), Pt - Rh catalyst speeds up the ____.
e: In the ammonia oxidation process (Ostwald process), Pt - Rh catalyst speeds up the reaction. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: The most well-known digestive enzymes, ptyalin in saliva and pepsin in gastric juice, catalyse to hasten the breakdown of large molecules, such as starch and protein, into simpler ____.
e: The most well-known digestive enzymes, ptyalin in saliva and pepsin in gastric juice, catalyse to hasten the breakdown of large molecules, such as starch and protein, into simpler molecules. Molecules is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The reaction between hydrogen and chlorine is extremely slow in the dark, but it becomes explosive when the reaction mixture is exposed to intense sunlight via a chain ____.
e: The reaction between hydrogen and chlorine is extremely slow in the dark, but it becomes explosive when the reaction mixture is exposed to intense sunlight via a chain reaction. Reaction is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
